remaining_concerns: The record available to this role still does not show current release documentation that reflects the current evaluation results for this release.
The record still does not show the actual disclosure text for the small-business onboarding weakness in the current release documentation.
No approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record is shown for the subgroup weakness.
Prior family approval and the informal monitoring comment remain contextual only and do not satisfy the policy predicate for current-release evidence or reviewed acceptance.
The Actor's narrowed theory is contingent on explicit disclosure, but that predicate is still unproven in the admissible record.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is analytically better than a clean-certification claim, but it still does not satisfy the decisive policy condition on the evidence available here: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The present record shows aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which are supportive, but those factors are not sufficient when the disclosure/mitigation predicate remains unresolved. This is the distinction between a caveated theory and compliant_with_caveats: a caveated theory can be reasonable in principle, but compliant_with_caveats still requires admissible evidence that the caveat has actually been implemented in the current release documentation or covered by approved mitigation. That evidence is not shown.
